newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade inactive - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade inactive - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade was quiet on Monday, with packers taking inventory of reduced feedlot supplies but not buying, feedlot sources said.
Bids ranged from $63.00 to $64.00 early and up to $65.00 late, but owners passed as they priced cattle mostly at $66.00, with some at $67.00 to $68.00, the sources said.

The majority of cattle last week sold at $65.00 in brisk trading that depleted showlists and scooped up the large number of cattle that feedlots had been unable to sell the previous week. Showlists this week were seen lighter following the hefty volume, they said.
Attempts to sell cattle at higher levels were rebuffed by lower CME live cattle futures following Friday's bearish USDA monthly cattle on feed report, the feedlot sources said.
The report showed a much larger than expected number of cattle being placed on feedlots during July. The report also showed greater than expected overall numbers of cattle on feed as of August 1.
The supply figures overshadowed potential support from active marketings during July, which kept feedlots extremely current, the sources said.
